result.summary: Round 2 (candidate-02) replaces candidate-01's 4-kernel eager chain (mul/add_/sub_/relu_, measured 10.239999741315842us) with a different, bounded direction: (a) the -0.125 shift is folded into the x-term via addcmul so scale+shift collapse into one pass, giving a 3-kernel eager chain, and (b) steady-state calls replay a captured CUDA graph keyed on the exact storage pointer / shape / stride / device / dtype of the incoming tensors, collapsing the chain into a single launch and removing the per-kernel gaps that dominate at 32x256 (8K elements = 32 KB). The baseline is 15.296000055968761us over six kernels (~2.5us/kernel), so latency is launch-bound, not math-bound: reducing dispatch count and inter-kernel gaps is the only lever that can move p50 materially. No file other than run.py was touched, and get_inputs/get_test_cases/get_benchmark_inputs/reference are preserved byte-for-byte; run(inputs) never writes to an input tensor, and the graph entry pins the input tensors so a replay can only read the current contents of the exact tensors passed in. Honest caveat: the stated 99.9999% target implies ~0.0000153us, which is physically unreachable for any real kernel; the candidate is submitted as a real, measurable step down from 10.24us with correctness preserved.

diagnosis.summary: At shape 32x256 the operator moves only 32 KB per tensor, so measured p50 tracks kernel count almost exactly (baseline 15.30us / 6 kernels, candidate-01 10.24us / 4 kernels, both ~2.5us per kernel). Arithmetic reformulation cannot help; only dispatch count and launch gaps can.
bottlenecks: Per-kernel launch + inter-kernel GPU gap (~2.5us each) dominates the 32 KB working set
Redundant output copy (.clone()) in the naive_v0 baseline
Separate scale, shift and activation passes that fuse into fewer TensorIterator passes
Python-side eager dispatch overhead on each op in the chain

Added an advisory CUDA-graph fast path: _capture() warms up the chain on a side stream, captures it under torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=side), replays once, and caches (graph, static_out, x, y) under a key of (x.data_ptr, y.data_ptr, x.shape, y.shape, x.stride, y.stride, x.device, y.device, x.dtype, y.dtype). A key is only captured after being seen twice, graph count is capped at 16 with no eviction (never frees a buffer a caller may still hold), and any failure, non-CUDA input, non-fp32 dtype, mismatched shapes, or nested capture falls back to the always-correct 3-kernel eager path.

candidateEvaluations.hypothesis: Because p50 is launch-bound at this shape, collapsing six kernels to three via addcmul, then collapsing the whole chain into one graph replay, should cut p50 well below candidate-01's 10.24us while keeping maxDiff inside atol/rtol 1e-5.
candidateEvaluations.change: In run(inputs): replaced the mul/add_/sub_/relu_ chain with _affine3(), which evaluates out = (-0.125) + x*1.25 in a single addcmul (cached 0-dim device scalars, broadcasting) then out + y*0.75 in a second addcmul(out=..., out=out) and a final in-place relu_() - 3 kernels, private output buffer, no clone. Added an advisory CUDA-graph fast path: _capture() warms up the chain on a side stream, captures it under torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=side), replays once, and caches (graph, static_out, x, y) under a key of (x.data_ptr, y.data_ptr, x.shape, y.shape, x.stride, y.stride, x.device, y.device, x.dtype, y.dtype). A key is only captured after being seen twice, graph count is capped at 16 with no eviction (never frees a buffer a caller may still hold), and any failure, non-CUDA input, non-fp32 dtype, mismatched shapes, or nested capture falls back to the always-correct 3-kernel eager path.
